issues.description: The `allocate` and `lock_range` verification boundaries trust their complete contracts because `allocate` fails a precondition and `lock_range` crashes Verus around `ManuallyDrop`.
issues.rationale: Collaborator rikosellic reports two concrete verification failures on the selected head: `allocate` encounters a failed precondition and `lock_range` triggers a Verus panic involving `ManuallyDrop`. The immediately following commit is explicitly named `Add external_body`, and the selected source marks both complete functions as external bodies. Consequently Verus assumes their postconditions without checking their implementations; callers may rely on `allocate` preserving the protocol/model state and on `lock_range` returning a well-formed write-locked cursor even though neither guarantee is established. The two manifestations are grouped because the review describes one deliberate whole-function trust-boundary workaround applied in the same commit and file.
